title: How Embodied Knowledge Moves, Fades, and Leaks
description: Classify four ways knowledge moves, fades or leaks, and separate intentional transfer from unintentional spillover.
creator: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
Knowledge Systems and Economic Complexity

educational.learningObjective: Given a central embodied-knowledge example, the learner will classify four ways that knowledge can move, fade, or transfer beyond its original holder, and distinguish cross-generational transfer (intentional) from knowledge spillover (unintentional).
prerequisites: Knows the difference between explicit and tacit knowledge
Has seen an organization lose capability when someone left
learningOutcomes: Distinguish intentional transfer from unintentional spillover
Explain why embodied knowledge does not transfer through documentation alone
educational.assessmentOpportunity: Give learners four short scenarios and ask which node each belongs to, with the intentional-versus-unintentional judgment stated explicitly.

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Click-to-explain hub-and-spoke diagram with color-coded categories
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Categorization with the distinction previewed by color before it is argued
pedagogical.feedbackType: A definition plus a distinct concrete example per node
misconceptionsAddressed: That knowledge can be fully captured in documentation
That all knowledge transfer is intentional
discussionQuestions: Why can a competitor copy a documented process and still fail to match the results?
Is knowledge spillover a cost to the firm or a benefit to the economy?
What would it cost to prevent decay in a capability you rarely use?
